Corporate History
We were incorporated in
the Cayman Islands on February 10, 2022 under the name Webus International Limited. Youbus International Limited (“Youbus International”),
our wholly-owned subsidiary, was incorporated in the British Virgin Islands on February 16, 2022. Webus Hongkong Limited (“Webus
HK”), a wholly-owned subsidiary of Youbus International, was incorporated in Hong Kong on February 22, 2022. Zhejiang Xinjieni
Technology Co., Ltd. (“WFOE”), Webus HK’s wholly owned subsidiary, was organized pursuant to Hong Kong law on August
31, 2022. Our variable interest entity, Zhejiang Youba Technology Co., Ltd., which we refer to as Youba Tech, was established on August
16, 2019 in Hangzhou, Zhejiang Province pursuant to PRC laws. Webus Travel Agency Co., Ltd., previously a wholly-owned subsidiary of
Youba Tech, was established on August 27, 2020 in Hangzhou, Zhejiang Province pursuant to PRC laws. We expanded its operations
to United States in March 2022 through Wetour Travel Tech LLC (“Wetour”), a limited liability company established in
Delaware pursuant to Delaware laws.
On September 7, 2022, the
Company consummated a reorganization pursuant to which, WFOE acquired a 50% equity interests in Youba Tech and entered into a series
of contractual arrangements for 50% VIE Interests with Youba Tech, as well as Individual Registered Shareholders. Wetour Robotics is
a holding company with no business operation other than holding the shares in Youbus International and Wetour, and Youbus International
is a pass-through entity with no business operation. WFOE is engaged in the business of managing the operation of Youba Tech and Webus
Travel Agency. Hangzhou Shunxing Technology Co., Ltd., a wholly-owned subsidiary of WFOE, which we refer to as Hangzhou Shunxing,
was established on June 10, 2025 in Hangzhou, Zhejiang Province pursuant to PRC laws.
On November 5, 2025, Youba
Tech transferred its 100% equity interest in Webus Travel Agency to Hangzhou Shunxing for a nominal consideration of RMB1. Following
the transfer, Webus Travel Agency became a wholly-owned subsidiary of Hangzhou Shunxing and an indirectly wholly-owned subsidiary of
the Company, and ceased to be a subsidiary of Youba Tech.
On December 9, 2025, we
established NextFood Technologies Inc. (“NextFood”) in the State of Delaware. On December 24, 2025, NextFood established
HeatBowl LLC (“HeatBowl”) as its subsidiary in the State of Texas.
On March 2, 2026, our shareholders
approved the change of the Company’s name Webus International Limited 微巴国际有限公司
to Wetour Robotics Limited. On March 9, 2026, the Company received from the Registrar of Companies of the Cayman Islands a Certificate
of Incorporation on Change of Name confirming that the Company’s name has been changed to Wetour Robotics Limited.
On March 19, 2026, HeatBowl LLC was
renamed to Vantrapower LLC to pursue transformer supply and power infrastructure opportunities for data centers, industrial facilities,
energy storage projects and other high-load applications. In September 2026, NextFood Technologies LLC transferred its 51% equity interest
in Vantrapower LLC to Wetour Travel Tech LLC. Following the transfer, Vantrapower LLC became a subsidiary of Wetour Travel Tech LLC and
ceased to be a subsidiary of NextFood Technologies Inc.
As of the date of this report,
we conduct our business operations by the VIE, Hangzhou Shunxing and Webus Travel Agency in China and our wholly owned subsidiaries Wetour,
NextFood and Vantrapower in United States. Our Physical AI platform development activities are principally conducted through
our United States subsidiaries including NextFood and Vantrapower.

Recent Developments
On February 27, 2026, we
held an extraordinary general meeting of shareholders, pursuant to the meeting our shareholders approved an increase in our authorized
share capital from US$50,000, divided into 500,000,000 ordinary shares of par value US$0.0001 each, to US$100,000, divided into 1,000,000,000
ordinary shares of the same par value. Our shareholders also approved the change of our name from “Webus International Limited
微巴国际有限公司 ”
to Wetour Robotics Limited. On March 9, 2026, we received from the Registrar of Companies of the Cayman Islands a Certificate of Incorporation
on Change of Name confirming that the Company’s name has been changed to Wetour Robotics Limited. In addition, the amended and
restated memorandum and articles of association reflecting the name change and increased authorized share capital was registered with
the Registrar and became in effect.
On March 2, 2026, we entered
into securities purchase agreements with ten purchasers for a private investment in public equity transaction in reliance on Regulation
S under the Securities Act of 1933, as amended (the “Securities Act”). Under these agreements, we agreed to issue and sell
60,000,000 ordinary shares of par value US$0.0001 each at US$0.086 per share, for aggregate gross proceeds of US$5,160,000. On March
18, 2026, we completed the closing of the transaction and issued the shares on March 18, 2026.
On March 17, 2026, we filed
a shelf registration statement on Form F-3 (File No. 333-294373) covering the offer and sale from time to time of up to US$100,000,000
of securities, including ordinary shares, share purchase contracts, share purchase units, warrants, debt securities, rights and units.
The registration statement was declared effective on March 30, 2026.
On April 30, 2026, we filed
a separate registration statement on Form F-3 (File No. 333-295457) to register the resale of 19,000,000 ordinary shares issued in the
March 2026 private placement by certain selling shareholders. The registration statement was declared effective on May 13, 2026. The
resale registration did not constitute an additional issuance of shares by us, and we would not receive proceeds from sales by the selling
shareholders.
On May 15, 2026, we entered
into the At Market Sales Agreement with Chaince Securities, LLC (“Chaince”). In accordance with the terms of the At Market
Sales Agreement, we may offer and sell our Ordinary Shares, having an aggregate offering price of up to $17,000,000 from time to time
through an at the market offering under which Chaince would as sales agent and/or principal. The offering has been registered under the
Securities Act pursuant to the Company’s shelf registration statement on Form F-3 (Registration No. 333-294373), as supplemented
by the prospectus supplement dated May 15, 2026. For sales in which Chaince acted as sales agent, we agreed to pay a commission equal
to 3.0% of gross proceeds and reimburse specified expenses. On July 6, 2026, we entered into Amendment No. 1 to the At Market Sales Agreement
with Chaince, to increase the maximum aggregate offering amount from US$17,000,000 to US$50,000,000.
On August 3, 2026, we effected
a 1-for-100 share consolidation, pursuant to the ordinary resolution passed by the shareholders of the Company at the extraordinary general
meeting held on February 27, 2026 and the board resolutions passed by the board of directors on July 6, 2026. As a result of the share
consolidation, every 100 ordinary shares of par value US$0.0001 each were consolidated into one ordinary share of par value US$0.01,
with fractional entitlements rounded up to the next whole share.

In addition to the other
information contained in this Annual Report and in other documents we file with or furnish to the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission
(the “SEC”), the following risk factors should be considered in evaluating our business. The occurrence of any of the events
or developments described below could materially harm our business, financial condition, results of operations and prospects. In such
an event, the market price of our ordinary shares could decline. Additional risks and uncertainties not presently known to us or that
we currently deem immaterial also may materially impair our business operations.
Summary of Risk Factors
Our business is subject
to a number of risks of which you should be aware before making an investment decision. Among these important risks are the following,
which are more fully described below:
Risks Related to Our Business and Industry
●
Demonstrations, early access programs,
evaluations and pilot projects involving our products may not result in commercial orders, broad deployments or recurring revenue.
●
Delays or difficulties in developing
and integrating the components of Orchestra could adversely affect our ability to commercialize our products and meet customer
requirements.
●
We have a limited operating history in
a competitive and rapidly evolving industry; and our transition toward Physical AI products may make it difficult to evaluate
our prospects and may expose us to significant execution risks.
●
We incurred net losses for the years
ended June 30, 2024, 2025 and 2026. We may not be able to generate sufficient operating cash flows and working capital. Failure
to manage our liquidity and cash flows may materially and adversely affect our financial condition and results of operations.
As a result, we may need additional capital, and financing may not be available on terms acceptable to us, or at all.
●
The growth of our business and our transition
toward Physical AI products depends on our ability to accurately anticipate market trends and customer demand and to develop
and commercialize new products and services that achieve market acceptance.
●
Our processing of physiological, visual
and interaction data may subject us to complex and evolving privacy, cybersecurity and data protection requirements, and any
actual or perceived failure to comply with such requirements or safeguard such data could adversely affect our business and customer
trust.
●
Hardware failures, component shortages
and difficulties supporting initial deployments could delay the commercialization of Orchestra and increase our costs and potential
liabilities.
●
The successful operation of our legacy
packaged tour services business depends substantially upon the cooperation of third parties that are not under our control.
●
We rely on search engines, social networking
sites and online streaming services to attract a meaningful portion of our users, and if those search engines, social networking
sites and online streaming services change their listings or policies regarding advertising, or increase their pricing or suffer
problems, it may limit our ability to attract new users.
●
Because we rely upon a third party to
perform the payment processing for our customers, the failure or inability of the third party to provide these services could
impair our ability to operate.
●
We may not be able to successfully implement
our growth strategy on a timely basis or at all.
●
Any damage to our reputation or our brands
may materially adversely affect our business, financial condition and results of operations.
●
We operate in a highly competitive industry
and may lose market share or experience margin erosion if we are unable to compete effectively.
●
Our operations in China are concentrated
in one geographic area, which increases our exposure to many of the risks enumerated herein.
●
We face risks associated with managing
operations in China, any of which could decrease our sales or earnings and could significantly limit or completely hinder our
ability to offer our Ordinary Shares to investors and cause the value of such securities to significantly decline or be worthless.
See “ Risk Factors — Risks Related
to Our Business” for more detailed disclosures on these risks and uncertainties.
Risks
Related to Corporate Structure
Risks
and uncertainties related to corporate structure include, but are not limited to, the following:
●
Wetour Robotics is a Cayman Islands exempted company operating in the
United States and in China partially through its subsidiaries and partially through contractual arrangements with the VIE. Investors thus
are not purchasing, and may never directly hold, 50% VIE Interests in the VIE. There are substantial uncertainties regarding the interpretation
and application of current and future PRC laws, regulations, and rules relating to the agreements that establish the VIE structure for
the majority of our and the VIE’s operations in China, including potential future actions by the PRC government, which could affect
the enforceability of our contractual arrangements with the VIE and, consequently, significantly affect the financial condition and results
of operations of Wetour Robotics. If the PRC government finds such agreements non-compliant with relevant PRC laws, regulations, and rules,
or if these laws, regulations, and rules or the interpretation thereof change in the future, we could be subject to severe penalties or
be forced to relinquish our interests in the VIE, which may materially and adversely affect our and the VIE’s operations and the
value of your investment.
●
We
are a holding company, and may rely on dividends paid by our subsidiaries for our cash needs. Any limitation on the ability of our subsidiaries
to make dividend payments to us, or any tax implications of making dividend payments to us, could limit our ability to pay for the holding
company expenses or pay dividends to holders of our Ordinary Shares.
●
We
rely on contractual arrangements with the VIE and Individual Registered Shareholders for our and the VIE’s operations in China,
which may not be as effective in providing operational control as direct ownership, and the VIE’s shareholders may fail to
perform their obligations under the contractual arrangements.
●
The
shareholders of the VIE may have conflicts of interests with us, which may materially and adversely affect our and the VIE’s
business.
●
The investors may face significant liquidity risks
because of the VIE structure and being based in and having the majority of the Company’s operations in China.
●
If we exercise the option to acquire equity ownership
and assets of the VIE, the ownership or asset transfer may subject us to certain limitations and substantial costs.
●
Certain
terms of the Contractual Arrangements may not be enforceable under PRC laws.
